subject: Cognitive Science
title: Fairness and Inequity Aversion
description: A quick, practical guide to Fairness and Inequity Aversion.

hook.text: Give two kids one cookie each—fine. Give one kid two? The other erupts. Fairness instinct is fierce.

buildup.text: By age three, children protest unequal splits. "That's not fair!" is one of the earliest moral claims.

discovery.text: Rejecting less for yourself appears first. Rejecting more than your share appears around age eight.

twist.text: Adults do it too. In the Ultimatum Game, people reject free money if the split feels unfair.

climax.text: Fairness overrides self-interest. People sacrifice personal gain to punish perceived inequality.

punchline.text: We'd rather lose than accept unfairness.

quiz.question: When does disadvantageous inequity aversion first appear?
